question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}, & x\ge 1,\,y\ge 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{X}(x)$ of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ g(x), & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $x\ge 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{y}]}_{y=1}^{y=b} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}{lim}_{b\to \infty }[1-\frac{1}{b}] \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $X$ for $x\ge 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}{f}_{X}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{x}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{u}]}_{1}^{x} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{x-1}{x},\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${F}_{X}(x)$ is

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ \frac{x-1}{x}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $g(x)=\frac{x-1}{x}.$
